# `kernel/SearchManager.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/SearchManager.js`

SearchManager.js — unified OS search backend for the command palette. Aggregates "app elements" from three kinds of sources, on top of the apps / subsurfaces / deep-links the palette already indexes: 1. Quick Actions (static)  — declared in a manifest's `actions` array. Each is a runnable item. If it carries a `command`, the palette dispatches it on the CommandBus; otherwise it is delivered to the app as an app-action (the app is opened/focused first, then receives ui:app-action / reads pendingActions). 2. Live content providers  — a running app registers a query callback via ui.registerSearchProvider(id, { label, query }). `query(q)` returns result items { id, label, sublabel?, icon?, run } where run() performs the action. Providers are same-realm closures, so run() can call straight back into the app. 3. Commands (opt-in)        — CommandBus commands registered with meta.search:true become searchable; selecting dispatches them (no-arg). Opt-in keeps destructive commands out of search by default. Events: ui:app-action { appId, actionId, args } — a manifest app-action was invoked.

| `cancelAction` | `cancelAction(appId, actionId, clientRequestId, provenance = null)` | Remove one exact, not-yet-consumed app action from the launch queue. Correlation is deliberately data-only: app code cannot pass a predicate into the kernel or cancel a neighbouring request that happens to share an action id. A false result means the action was never queued or has already crossed the mounting app's `pendingActions()` boundary. |
| `actionDeliveryState` | `actionDeliveryState(appId, actionId, clientRequestId, provenance = null)` | Return the authoritative lifecycle state of one correlated app action. |
| `requeueActionDelivery` | `requeueActionDelivery(appId, actionId, clientRequestId)` | Move one exact receiver-owned in-flight action back to its queue unchanged. |
| `discardActionDeliveries` | `discardActionDeliveries(appId)` | Discard every delivery owned by an app whose mount failed terminally. |
| `settleActionDelivery` | `settleActionDelivery(appId, actionId, clientRequestId)` | Settle one correlated action after its receiving app admits or rejects it. |
| `takeActions` | `takeActions(appId)` | Take (and clear) actions queued for an app that is mounting now. |

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
